That the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Companygonj, Sylhet in violation of the above mentioned memo dated 17.10.1985 initiated Miscellaneous Case No.147 of 2004-2005 under section 92(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for taking over 1.54 acres of land out of that 20 acres of land under khas khatian No.1 of the Government and in that miscellaneous case by the impugned order dated 22.03.2005 the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Companygonj, Sylhet treated the aforesaid 1.54 acres of land as khas land of the Government with a direction to the concerned officials to take over possession of the same. 

 6. The respondent No.1 opposed that rule. The material case of the respondent No.1 was that though the predecessors of the writ petitioners took lease of the land in question from the government for a period of 25 years the writ petitioners did not take any step for renewal of the said lease after expiry of that 25 years and as such the lease deed lost its validity after that period; that the government cancelled that decision in respect of non-renewal of long term lease and as such there was no illegality in starting Miscellaneous Case No. 147 of 2004-2005 under section 92(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the impugned order passed therein. It was also alleged from the side of the contesting respondent that the writ petition was not maintainable since the writ petitioners did not challenge the impugned order by filing a suit in civil court as per section 29(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The High Court Division, after hearing the learned Counsel of both the sides and examining and considering the relevant annexure made the rule absolute declaring the impugned miscellaneous case and the impugned order passed therein illegal and directed the respondents to renew the long term lease of the land in question in favour of the writ petitioners and to receive rents from the writ petitioners regularly. 

 7. Mr. Rajik-Al-Jalil, the Deputy Attorney General has made submissions before us on behalf of the leave petitioners. He has mainly argued that there was no illegality in starting the Miscellaneous Case No. 147 of 2004-205 for the purpose of declaring the land in question as khas land as per provision of section 92(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act since the period of long term lease expired, that the High Court Division has failed to appreciate this legal position and as such has arrived at a wrong decision which is liable to be interfered by this Division. The learned advocate has argued also that for the greater public interest the lease granted in favour of the predecessor of the writ petitioners was cancelled and that the government has right to cancel this temporary lease and also make the abandoned property as khas property of the government and in the circumstance the High Court Division committed error of law in declaring the impugned order illegal and also directing the respondents to renew the lease in favour of the writ petitioners. 

 11. We do not find any wrong or illegality in the above findings of the High Court Division. Admittedly, the writ petitioners have been possessing the land in question as lessees for a long period of more then 25 years. Their predecessors took lease of this land by registered deeds of lease in the year 1975 and possessed the same peacefully on payment of rent and after them the writ petitioners have been possessing the said land on payment of rent regularly. There is no allegation that the writ petitioners or their predecessors ever violated any terms and conditions the lease deed. Rather, admittedly, as per terms of the lease deeds the writ petitioners applied for renewal of the lease deed for a further period of 25 years and that application was not rejected till date by the concerned authority. In the circumstance the initiative of the respondents for taking possessing of 1.54 acres of land out of that lease-hold 20 acres of land from the writ petitioners has been illegal. The writ petitioners, admittedly, were not served with any notice before passing the impugned order for taking back 1.54 acres of their lease-hold lands from them. This has also violated the principle of natural justice. The High Court Division did not accept also the contesting respondent's plea that the writ petition was not maintainable since sub-section (4) of section 92 of the State Acquisitions and Tenancy Act has provided that the aggrieved person may file a suit before the civil court against any order under section 92(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The respondent's contention was that the impugned order was passed under section 92(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as such it can be assailed by filing a suit before the civil court. But this contention of the respondents was not accepted by the High Court Division on the finding that since by the impugned order the fundamental right of the writ petitioners to their lease-hold land was infringed the petitioners were entitled to come directly to the High Court Division with the application under Article 102 of the Constitution. However, we find also that none of the circumstances as embodied in section 92(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was existing and as such the impugned Miscellaneous Case No.147 of 2004-2005 cannot be a proceeding under section 92(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In the circumstances the writ petition cannot be said to be not maintainable.
